newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai banker says speedy reforms can be dangerous.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker says speedy reforms can be dangerous.

text.p: Bangkok Bank Plc president Chartsiri Sophonpanich on Monday warned Asian emerging economies from plunging into liberalisation and deregulation as a short-cut to rapid growth.

"It is true that such a policy is quite appealing with many attractive features. However, the truth on the darker side has not been clearly revealed until recently," Sophonpanich said at a forum of Asian businessmen.
Thailand, which enjoyed high growth rates in recent years, is currently in the grip of an economic crisis, triggered by a collapse in the real estate and banking sectors.

Sophonpanich said he was not discouraging developing countries from opening up their economies, but said they should be extra cautious in allowing short-term foreign capital to drive their domestic economies.

"For small developing coutnries in the Asia-Pacific region, we are handicapped in numerous aspects and are limited in strength to compete successfully in the open world market. To pretend that we are good or strong enough will only bring us nothing but disappointment and misery," he said.
Sophonpanich said easy access to foreign funds at cheaper rates often lead to careless investment decisions.
"Over investment in the real estate business and stock market speculation are certainly the most common culprits of this misuse of foreign capital," he said.
This will lead to rising national debt, deficit in current account and creeping inflation. He said Indonesia, India and the Philippines are prone to this particular risk.
"In the emerging market, where the economy is still immature, a fast pace of development may very well throw the system off-balance," he said.

"Removing of barriers for free competition will have to be made gradually, step by step, according to the prevailing market structure. There is no better alternative to slow but sure growth with stability," Sophonpanich added.
